# runpod_pod_action (Resource)

Runs one state transition on an existing pod. This resource is imperative, not declarative: it holds no pod state and reconciles nothing. The action runs when the resource is created, and again whenever action or triggers change. A refresh calls nothing, so a pod that changes state on its own produces no diff, and destroying the resource only forgets it: the pod is left as it is.

Do not use it on a pod whose runpod_pod resource sets desired_state: that attribute manages the same transitions declaratively and would fight this one, each apply undoing the other. Pick desired_state for a run state Terraform should keep, and this resource for a one-off restart or a stop tied to something else changing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Restart the pod whenever the image it should run changes. The action is
# imperative: it runs on create and on every triggers change, and destroying
# this resource leaves the pod as it is.
resource "runpod_pod_action" "restart_on_image_change" {
  pod_id = runpod_pod.jupyter.id
  action = "restart"

  triggers = {
    image = var.image
  }
}

# Stop a pod on demand. Do not combine this with runpod_pod.desired_state on
# the same pod: desired_state manages the run state declaratively, and the two
# would undo each other on every apply.
resource "runpod_pod_action" "stop_overnight" {
  pod_id = runpod_pod.batch.id
  action = "stop"

  triggers = {
    shift = var.shift
  }
}
```

Complete, runnable configurations that use this resource live in the use-case
modules under `v2/modules/` in the provider repository; the Guides section
documents each one.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) Transition to run: start boots a stopped pod, stop releases its compute but keeps the disk, restart restarts the container in place, terminate deletes the pod permanently. Which ones are valid depends on the pod's current status, and the API rejects the rest with a conflict. Changing this re-runs the action.
- `pod_id` (String) Pod to act on. Pointing the resource at a different pod replaces it, which runs the action on the new pod and leaves the old one untouched.

### Optional

- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that re-run the action when any of them changes. This is the usual way to restart a pod after an image tag, template, or config value moves. Adding, removing, or changing an entry runs the action again.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The pod this resource acts on; there is one action runner per pod.
- `status` (String) Pod status the action returned, as the 1.x resource reported it: PROVISIONING, STARTING, RUNNING, EXITED, ERROR, or TERMINATED. It is the status at the moment the action was accepted, not a live value: a transition the API takes asynchronously still reads as the status before it lands, and a refresh does not update it. terminate answers with no body, so it leaves this null.
